recipes.title: Lomo Saltado
recipes.dish_alt: A plate of Peruvian lomo saltado, stir-fried beef strips with tomato and red onion, served with white rice.
recipes.prep_alt: Lomo saltado plated with crisp French fries tucked into the beef and tomato stir-fry alongside rice.

sections.heading: Ingredients by Serving
rows: Beef sirloin, sliced into thin strips

sections.heading: Steps
items: Season the beef strips with salt and pepper. If using frozen fries, cook according to package directions until crisp; keep warm.
Heat the oil in a wok or large skillet over very high heat until just smoking. Sear the beef in batches, 1–2 minutes, until browned outside but still pink inside. Remove to a plate.
Add the onion to the same pan and cook 1–2 minutes, until just softened but still a little crisp.
Add the garlic and ají amarillo paste, cooking 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the tomato wedges, soy sauce, and vinegar, tossing 1–2 minutes until the tomato just starts to break down and release its juices.
Return the beef and the fries to the pan and toss everything together for 1 minute, just to combine and reheat — don't let the fries sit in the sauce long or they'll go soft.
Sprinkle with cilantro and serve immediately with white rice on the side.

recipes.title: Ají de Gallina
recipes.dish_alt: A plate of aji de gallina, creamy yellow shredded-chicken sauce, next to white rice, garnished with black olives.
recipes.prep_alt: Aji de gallina served over sliced boiled potato with rice and a hard-boiled egg wedge on the side.

sections.heading: Steps
items: Poach the chicken breast in salted simmering water 15–18 minutes until cooked through; reserve some of the poaching liquid as broth. Once cool enough to handle, shred the chicken finely.
Soak the torn bread in the evaporated milk for 5 minutes until soft.
Blend the soaked bread (with its milk), toasted walnuts, and parmesan until smooth. Set aside.
Heat the oil in a pot over medium heat. Add the onion and cook 5–6 minutes until soft.
Add the garlic and ají amarillo paste, cooking 2 minutes until fragrant and deep gold.
Stir in the walnut-bread mixture and the reserved chicken broth, whisking until smooth.
Add the shredded chicken, stir to coat, and simmer 8–10 minutes, stirring often, until thick and creamy — it should look like a loose, glossy béchamel.
Season with salt to taste.
Spoon over sliced boiled potato and rice; garnish each plate with hard-boiled egg and black olives.

recipes.title: Ceviche Clásico
recipes.dish_alt: A bowl of Peruvian ceviche clasico, cubed white fish and shrimp cured in lime with red onion, corn, and sweet potato.
recipes.prep_alt: Cubed white fish curing in lime juice with sliced red onion and chile, plated with corn and sweet potato.

sections.heading: Ingredients by Serving
rows: White fish fillet (sea bass, tilapia, or halibut), cubed
Ají limo, rocoto, or serrano chile, thinly sliced
Sweet potato, boiled, sliced, to serve
Corn on the cob (choclo), boiled, to serve

sections.heading: Steps
items: Pat the fish cubes dry, place in a non-reactive bowl, and season generously with salt.
Add the garlic and half the red onion; toss to combine.
Pour over the lime juice, making sure all the fish is submerged. Let it cure 5–10 minutes at room temperature — just until the fish turns opaque; longer isn't better here, the fish can turn rubbery.
Add the sliced chile and cilantro, and toss gently.
Taste the citrus marinade (leche de tigre) and adjust salt — it should be bright, salty-sour, and a little spicy.
Pile the ceviche onto plates with plenty of the citrus liquid, and top with the remaining red onion.
Serve immediately alongside the boiled sweet potato and a piece of corn.

recipes.title: Arroz con Pollo Peruano
recipes.dish_alt: A mound of green cilantro rice next to a roasted chicken quarter, Peruvian arroz con pollo verde.
recipes.prep_alt: Golden arroz con pollo peruano with chicken drumsticks over rice, plated with a tomato and onion side salad.

sections.heading: Steps
items: Blend the cilantro with a splash of the chicken stock until smooth; set aside.
Season the chicken with salt and pepper. Heat the oil in a pot over medium-high heat and brown the chicken 3–4 minutes per side. Remove.
In the same pot, add the onion, garlic, and bell pepper; cook 4–5 minutes until softened.
Stir in the ají amarillo paste and cook 1 minute.
Add the rice, stirring to coat it in the fat, then pour in the cilantro purée and the remaining chicken stock.
Nestle the chicken back into the pot, add the carrot, and bring to a simmer.
Cover and cook on low 18–20 minutes until the rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed.
Stir in the peas, cover, and rest off the heat for 5 minutes.
Fluff with a fork and serve hot.

recipes.title: Seco de Res
recipes.dish_alt: A bowl of seco de res, Peruvian beef and cilantro stew, with red onion and rice.
recipes.prep_alt: Seco de res beef stew plated with canary beans (frejoles) and white rice.

sections.heading: Ingredients by Serving
rows: Dark beer (substitute for chicha de jora)

sections.heading: Steps
items: Blend the cilantro with a splash of beef stock until smooth; set aside.
Season the beef with salt and pepper. Heat the oil in a heavy pot over medium-high heat and brown the beef in batches, 3–4 minutes per side. Remove.
In the same pot, add the onion and garlic, cooking 5–6 minutes until soft.
Stir in the ají amarillo paste, cooking 1–2 minutes until fragrant.
Return the beef to the pot, pour in the beer, and let it bubble 1–2 minutes to cook off the raw alcohol smell.
Add the cilantro purée and beef stock, and bring to a simmer.
Cover and cook on low 35–40 minutes until the beef is nearly fork-tender.
Add the potato and carrot, cover, and cook 15 minutes more until the vegetables and beef are tender.
Stir in the peas and simmer uncovered 5 minutes to thicken slightly. Season with salt.
Serve hot with white rice.

recipes.title: Causa Rellena
recipes.dish_alt: A log of causa rellena, layered chilled potato with chicken filling and avocado, garnished with olives.
recipes.prep_label: Prep & Plating — Layered Potato, Avocado & Chicken
recipes.prep_alt: A stack of causa rellena showing the layers of golden aji-amarillo potato, avocado, and chicken salad.

sections.heading: Ingredients by Serving
rows: Yellow or Yukon Gold potatoes, boiled and riced

sections.heading: Steps
items: Rice or mash the boiled potatoes while still warm until completely smooth and lump-free.
Mix in the ají amarillo paste, lime juice, oil, and salt until the potato is a vivid gold and holds together like a soft dough. Let it cool to room temperature.
Meanwhile, mix the shredded chicken with the mayonnaise and celery to make the filling.
Line a small loaf pan or ring mold with plastic wrap. Press in half the potato mixture in an even layer.
Layer the avocado slices over the potato, then spread the chicken filling on top, then the tomato slices.
Press in the remaining potato mixture to seal, smoothing the top.
Cover and refrigerate at least 1 hour, until firm and cold.
Unmold, slice, and garnish with the sliced hard-boiled egg and black olives just before serving.

recipes.title: Pollo a la Brasa with Ají Verde
recipes.dish_alt: Peruvian roast pollo a la brasa chicken with crisp golden skin, plated with fries and a carrot garnish.
recipes.prep_label: Prep & Plating — Roast Chicken with Rice
recipes.prep_alt: Roasted pollo a la brasa chicken plated with rice and salad, ready to serve with aji verde sauce.

sections.heading: Chicken & Marinade
rows: Ají panca paste (or smoked paprika + pinch cayenne)

sections.heading: Steps
items: Whisk together the marinade ingredients — garlic, soy sauce, ají panca, lime juice, cumin, oregano, oil, salt, and pepper.
Rub the marinade all over the chicken thighs, including under the skin. Marinate at least 30 minutes at room temperature, or up to overnight in the fridge.
Meanwhile, blend all the ají verde ingredients until smooth; taste and adjust salt or lime. Refrigerate until serving.
Heat the oven to 220°C (425°F), or heat a grill pan over medium-high.
Roast the chicken thighs skin-side up 30–35 minutes (or grill 6–7 minutes per side), basting once with the pan juices, until the skin is deeply burnished and a thermometer reads 74°C (165°F).
Rest 5 minutes, then serve with the ají verde sauce alongside.

recipes.title: Picarones
recipes.dish_alt: Two golden fried picarones rings drizzled with dark chancaca syrup on a white plate.
recipes.prep_alt: Picarones dough rings frying in a pot of hot oil, turning golden brown.

sections.heading: Chancaca Syrup
rows: Dark brown sugar, panela, or piloncillo, chopped

sections.heading: Steps
items: Boil the squash and sweet potato until fork-tender, about 15 minutes; drain and mash until smooth.

In a large bowl, mix the flour, sugar, yeast, anise seed, and salt. Stir in the mashed squash and sweet potato, adding warm water a little at a time, until you have a soft, sticky, elastic dough — about the consistency of a thick pancake batter you could still pinch into a ring.
Cover and let rise in a warm spot about 1 hour, until doubled and bubbly.
Meanwhile, make the chancaca syrup: simmer the chopped panela, water, cinnamon stick, cloves, and orange peel 10–12 minutes until syrupy. Strain and set aside.
Heat oil to 350°F (175°C) in a deep pot.
Wet your hand or a spoon, scoop a portion of dough, and shape it into a ring directly into the hot oil (or drop it as a rustic free-form dollop if shaping rings feels fiddly).
Fry 2–3 minutes per side until deep golden and crisp, working in batches so the oil temperature doesn't drop.
Drain on a rack or paper towels. Drizzle warm with the chancaca syrup and serve immediately.
